identity_entries.value: motivation pp. 1–3; interface pp. 3–6; evaluation pp. 5–11; limitations and boundary conditions pp. 10–12.
quotes: "We aimed to build a system to support BLV users in identifying unreliable information in MLLM-generated responses and assessing model reliability." (p. 3)

"To gather BLV people’s perceptions of variations, we develop a study prototype that automatically aligns and presents variations guided by our design choices and accessibility considerations for generative AI systems [59, 76]." (p. 4)

"We conducted a within-subject study with 15 BLV participants to investigate how surfacing variations in MLLM-generated image descriptions impacts BLV users’ ability to recognize unreliable claims in MLLM responses and their perceived reliability of MLLM responses." (p. 5)
"Our system currently supports surfacing variations in static image descriptions." (p. 12)

rq3_entries.value: the system decomposes responses into atomic facts, groups semantically corresponding claims, constructs a hierarchy, and derives a concise cross-model summary (PDF p. 5).
quotes: "We employ Chain-of-Thought [75] and few-shot prompting techniques to instruct Gemini-2.5-pro to decompose each description into atomic facts and reassemble them into coherent, logically structured text." (p. 5)
"Finally, we transform the variation-aware description into a more concise variation summary that highlights agreements, disagreements, and unique mentions across models." (p. 5)

rq3_entries.value: the user still identifies potentially unreliable claims and explains the judgment (PDF p. 7).
quotes: "For each image, participants had up to 4 minutes to verbally report any unreliable parts of the description(s) and explain their reasoning." (p. 7)

rq3_entries.value: the study measured immediate unreliable-claim reports and perceptions of description quality, coverage, and trustworthiness, not learning or transfer (PDF p. 7).
quotes: "Afterward, they answered questions about their perception of the description’s quality [53], information coverage [53], and trustworthiness [32]." (p. 7)

rq3_entries.value: author_raised — the authors identify uncommunicated errors as a source of over-reliance (PDF p. 11).
quotes: "The absence of a mechanism to communicate errors in current MLLM-powered access technologies may lead to users’ over-reliance on AI." (p. 11)

rq3_entries.value: no — users may hide an indicator, but the system does not withdraw support as competence grows (PDF p. 5).
quotes: "In the variation-aware description, users can toggle how the degree of support for variants is displayed (Table 2)." (p. 5)

rq3_entries.value: users must inspect the descriptions, report unreliable parts, explain their reasoning, and decide whether details matter or require clarification (PDF pp. 7, 10).
quotes: "For each image, participants had up to 4 minutes to verbally report any unreliable parts of the description(s) and explain their reasoning." (p. 7)
"P10 says that “you can look at the disagreements, check if those details don’t matter or that’s super relevant steers to whether you need clarification or not.”" (p. 10)

rq3_entries.value: single_session (1) — each participant completed one 1.5-hour session (PDF p. 7).
quotes: "Each study session lasted 1.5 hours and was conducted one-on-one over Zoom." (p. 7)

claim_entries.value: surfacing variations improves BLV users’ identification of unreliable information and lowers perceived reliability of MLLM descriptions (PDF p. 12).
quotes: "Our user study findings demonstrate that surfacing variations across MLLM-generated image descriptions significantly improves blind and low vision users’ ability to identify unreliable information and decreases their perceived reliability of MLLM descriptions." (p. 12)

claim_entries.value: within_subject — the same participants experienced the description conditions (PDF p. 5).
quotes: "We conducted a within-subject study with 15 BLV participants to investigate how surfacing variations in MLLM-generated image descriptions impacts BLV users’ ability to recognize unreliable claims in MLLM responses and their perceived reliability of MLLM responses." (p. 5)

claim_entries.value: 15 — all were BLV screen-reader users with prior MLLM visual-access experience (PDF p. 6).
quotes: "We recruited 15 BLV participants who regularly use screen readers to access online content and have prior experience with MLLM-powered visual access tools for image descriptions (Table 3)." (p. 6)

claim_entries.value: target_practitioners — participants were members of the intended user population and regular users of the relevant tools (PDF p. 6).
quotes: "We recruited 15 BLV participants who regularly use screen readers to access online content and have prior experience with MLLM-powered visual access tools for image descriptions (Table 3)." (p. 6)

claim_entries.value: control_condition — single, list, and combined aggregate conditions were counterbalanced (PDF p. 7).
quotes: "For each image, participants used one of three description conditions (single, list, ours), and we counterbalanced description conditions across the three ambiguity sources such that participants used each description condition 3 times, once for each ambiguity source." (p. 7)

claim_entries.value: test_only — inferential tests and corrected pairwise comparisons were reported without a standardized effect size (PDF p. 8).
quotes: "We applied the Friedman test followed by pairwise Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Bonferroni correction." (p. 8)
"Each study session lasted 1.5 hours and was conducted one-on-one over Zoom." (p. 7)

claim_entries.value: the detailed aggregate overwhelmed three participants, and the raw list imposed excessive information-processing demands for most participants (PDF p. 10).
quotes: "While many participants love the comprehensiveness of variation-aware description, others (P2, P6, P11) feel overwhelmed when going through all of the details." (p. 10)
"However, the rest 13 participants unanimously pointed out that there was too much information to process in the list presentation style, especially for screen readers." (p. 10)

claim_entries.value: within the tested single-session task, the controlled comparison supports the stated performance and perceived-reliability claim; it does not establish longitudinal learning or deployed-use effects (PDF p. 8).
quotes: "Overall, surfacing variations in MLLM responses increased the number of unreliable claims identified (RQ1) in MLLM descriptions by 4.9x for ours (M = 2.62, SD = 1.72) or 4.2x for list (M = 2.24, SD = 1.52) compared to presenting a single description (M = 0.53, SD = 0.73) (Tabe 4)." (p. 8)

paper_code_entries.value: nonvisual verification and trust calibration of MLLM-generated image descriptions for blind and low-vision users (PDF p. 1).
quotes: "We explore how systematically surfacing variations across multiple MLLM responses can support BLV users to detect unreliable information without visually inspecting the image." (p. 1)

paper_code_entries.value: immediate_performance_or_sensemaking — the support helps users judge current descriptions rather than develop a taught skill (PDF p. 3).
quotes: "We aimed to build a system to support BLV users in identifying unreliable information in MLLM-generated responses and assessing model reliability." (p. 3)

paper_code_entries.value: evaluation_or_judgment_gap — BLV users cannot directly compare the visual source with a generated description to assess correctness (PDF p. 2).
quotes: "BLV people are early adopters of AI technologies [21], but assessing visual descriptions’ correctness remains challenging, as they cannot directly visually verify the descriptions against the image." (p. 2)

paper_code_entries.value: process — the study measures users’ recognition of unreliable claims and perceived reliability during the verification task (PDF p. 5).
quotes: "We conducted a within-subject study with 15 BLV participants to investigate how surfacing variations in MLLM-generated image descriptions impacts BLV users’ ability to recognize unreliable claims in MLLM responses and their perceived reliability of MLLM responses." (p. 5)

paper_code_entries.value: structuring — semantically aligned outputs are reorganized into a coherent navigable hierarchy (PDF p. 4).
quotes: "The variation-aware description (Figure 2C) presents an aggregated detail summary in a hierarchical, coherent markdown format to support a detailed understanding of variations." (p. 4)

paper_code_entries.value: problematizing — the overview explicitly brings conflicts and isolated claims to the user’s attention (PDF p. 5).
quotes: "The variation summary (Figure 2D) builds on the aggregated summary by explicitly highlighting areas of agreement, disagreement, and unique mentions across models to support quick surface of key variations across all descriptions." (p. 5)

paper_code_entries.value: distributed_support — comparison evidence is assembled from several MLLM sources rather than one response (PDF p. 3).
quotes: "Informed by their current practice, and prior work that indicates exposing sighted users to multiple LLM responses reduces trust [52], we seek to support BLV users easily surfacing and comparing multiple responses from MLLMs at once." (p. 3)

paper_code_entries.value: hybrid_or_multi_model — three MLLMs generate descriptions and another MLLM organizes them (PDF p. 5).
quotes: "We select 3 state-of-the-art MLLMs, namely GPT-4o, Claude 3.7 Sonnet, and Gemini 1.5 Pro, to generate image descriptions." (p. 5)

paper_code_entries.value: llm_era — the scaffold’s meaning is produced from MLLM-generated image descriptions (PDF p. 5).
quotes: "We then generate the variation-aware description based on the MLLM-generated image descriptions (Figure 1)." (p. 5)

limitations: "While many participants love the comprehensiveness of variation-aware description, others (P2, P6, P11) feel overwhelmed when going through all of the details." (p. 10)
"Participants in our study did not opt to test our system on people." (p. 12)
"However, conveying variation in real-time video streams may be difficult, as reading out variations requires time on an already time-limited medium." (p. 12)
boundary_conditions: "Our system currently supports surfacing variations in static image descriptions." (p. 12)
"We recruited 15 BLV participants who regularly use screen readers to access online content and have prior experience with MLLM-powered visual access tools for image descriptions (Table 3)." (p. 6)
"We selected 9 challenging image–prompt pairs that include ambiguity and reflect common use scenarios for BLV MLLM users (Figure 3)." (p. 6)
"Each study session lasted 1.5 hours and was conducted one-on-one over Zoom." (p. 7)
"We plan to deploy variation-aware descriptions in the wild to further understand usage scenarios and user preferences in context." (p. 12)
